records.notes: Measured on ryzen9900x-8t-32g. security_bits=128 is claimed by the implementation and is published as a label only — it is not verified here. The online answer therefore touches one 2048-record shard no matter how large the database is, and ClientQuery.shard_id is sent in cleartext, so the server learns which shard the query is in. records.notes: Measured on ryzen9900x-8t-32g. security_bits=128 is claimed by the implementation and is published as a label only — it is not verified here. Scheme params are whatever this implementation chose; compare across implementations with that in mind. CAVEAT: Inherits the upstream's behaviour: query() regenerates InspiRING packing keys on every call, so client_query_gen_ms and query_bytes include per-query key generation and shipping. inspire-raven's do not. CODE PATH: in this codebase respond_with_variant() dispatches OnePacking and TwoPacking to the same function (respond_inspiring), so requesting TwoPacking actually runs InsPIRe^1, not InsPIRe^2. Raven's fork patched this exact fall-through. The row is therefore not executing the same algorithm as inspire-raven's TwoPacking row even though both are labelled two-packing. CAVEAT: Run with 1 seed x 4 measured iterations instead of the 3 x 16 used for inspire-raven. This implementation's per-query cost is ~2000x higher (4.0 s vs 1.9 ms at 2^20 x 8 B on the reference machine), so the default counts are unfinishable at the larger cells. Fewer iterations lowers confidence in the number; it does not change what is being measured. The counts actually used are recorded in params.scheme_params. A second fork of the deleted igor53627/inspire-rs, diverged 2026-04-24 — after the upstream's last substantive commit but before Raven's patches. Declares the same crate name and version (inspire 0.2.0) and exports an identical public API, so it is benchmarked through the same shared driver as inspire-upstream; the interesting question is whether the fork changed anything measurable. Last pushed 2026-04-24.

records.notes: Measured on ryzen9900x-8t-32g. security_bits=128 is claimed by the implementation and is published as a label only — it is not verified here. Scheme params are whatever this implementation chose; compare across implementations with that in mind. CAVEAT: poulpy's example averages the online phase over its own REPEATS=10 and exposes no seed parameter, so this row reports a single run with no cross-seed spread, where the raven and upstream rows report a median over 3 seeds. client_decode_ms is not reported by the example and is omitted rather than invented. Independent implementation of InsPIRe on the Poulpy FHE library — not a fork of inspire-rs. Interpolation construction (the direct analogue of the other InsPIRe rows here); the recursive InsPIRe² construction is published separately as inspire2-poulpy because it is a different protocol, not a tuning knob. Requires AVX-512F: the crate's avx512-fhe feature has a compile-time guard and only builds on an AVX-512 host. Database layouts follow the crate's DefaultPirParameters32B presets, which are 32-byte payloads only at 1/2/4/8/16/32 GiB — mapping to entries_log2 25..30. The cols choice per size follows the crate's own examples/README pairing.

CAVEAT: Upstream 0.2.0's query() calls maybe_generate_packing_keys() on EVERY query — there is no session or key-cache API. Raven's fork added pir/session.rs (ClientSession + a packing-key pre-exchange handshake, keys uploaded once and referenced by handle). So client_query_gen_ms and query_bytes for this row include per-query InspiRING key generation and shipping, while inspire-raven's do not. That is a real difference between the implementations, not a harness artifact — but the two per-query numbers are not measuring the same work, and any comparison must say so. CODE PATH: in this codebase respond_with_variant() dispatches OnePacking and TwoPacking to the same function (respond_inspiring), so requesting TwoPacking actually runs InsPIRe^1, not InsPIRe^2. Raven's fork patched this exact fall-through. The row is therefore not executing the same algorithm as inspire-raven's TwoPacking row even though both are labelled two-packing. CAVEAT: Run with 1 seed x 4 measured iterations instead of the 3 x 16 used for inspire-raven. This implementation's per-query cost is ~2000x higher (4.0 s vs 1.9 ms at 2^20 x 8 B on the reference machine), so the default counts are unfinishable at the larger cells. Fewer iterations lowers confidence in the number; it does not change what is being measured. The counts actually used are recorded in params.scheme_params. Its secure_128_d2048 uses the 2-CRT moduli [268369921, 249561089] (q ~ 2^56), which is exactly the parameter set Raven's fork replaced with a single-prime q = 2^60 - 2^14 + 1, calling it under-provisioned.
